name: What questions should I ask about office build-out financing or cash flow?

mainEntity.name: How should I plan cash flow if the landlord allowance is reimbursed after construction instead of paid upfront?
mainEntity.text: How should I plan cash flow if the landlord allowance is reimbursed after construction instead of paid upfront?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cash flow can become a major issue when a landlord allowance is reimbursed after completion instead of paid upfront. In that situation, the tenant often has to cover design, permits, construction billing, and possibly furniture or technology costs before reimbursement arrives. The lease should clarify what documentation is required, when reimbursements are processed, and whether retainage or inspection sign-off is needed first. Tenants in Los Angeles-area office build-outs should also consider whether the contractor expects progress payments and how that aligns with landlord reimbursement timing. If the cash gap is too large, the project may need a financing plan or a phased schedule. Reviewing payment timing before signing the lease is one of the easiest ways to avoid a funding shortfall mid-project.
acceptedAnswer.description: If the allowance is reimbursed after completion, tenants may need enough cash to pay design, permit, and construction costs before getting paid back. It is important to confirm the reimbursement timing, documentation requirements, and whether any retainage or holdback applies.
